cases.input: Build marketing agents to draft an email and landing page from five approved documents. No ongoing monitoring is needed.
expect: Map product facts, customer evidence, and channel constraints before naming executors.
Recommend one capable harness with tools as the first slice; no mandatory bus or containers.
Specify source evidence, approval boundaries, and measurable quality/cost/latency baseline.
reject: Default CMO/sales/support org chart.
More agents asserted to outperform one harness without evidence.

cases.input: Keep a migration plan current across 200 changing packages and dependency notices; one coding harness executes it.
expect: Partition maintained contexts by source/domain boundaries, not persona labels.
Track source versions, evidence, freshness, coverage gaps, and decision subscriptions.
Keep unrelated changes quiet and justify observer concurrency independently of executor count.
reject: One executor per package by default.
File hash described as semantic symbol identity.

cases.input: Run independent Linux and Windows build validation under different credentials before a short deadline, then produce one recommendation.
expect: Consider multiple executors for independent work, dependencies, permissions, and measured latency.
Share versioned awareness/evidence contract while isolating execution and enforcing an application result gate.
Compare coordination cost with the single-harness baseline.
reject: Forbid multiple executors categorically.
Grant release authority through a role prompt.

cases.input: An active draft subscribes to product A. Observe a valid product B change outside its dependencies.
expect: Update B's context/version and freshness with recorded relevance decision.
No alert or executor invocation for the A draft within the configured reconciliation window.
reject: Broadcast every change.
Discard B's observation entirely because no consumer is interested.

cases.input: Withdraw a product claim currently cited by an active draft.
expect: One logical alert carries stable event/correlation IDs, current source version, evidence pointer, impact, and intended consumer.
Consumer fetches authorized evidence and acknowledges a validated revision or rejection with the version used.
reject: Count accepted transport or a mention as semantic attention.
Treat thread membership as task assignment.

cases.input: Deliver the same event twice with different Coral message IDs; also remove and re-add a participant so history replays.
expect: Unique consumer/event identity deduplicates logical handling across both paths.
At most one committed product effect; repeated acknowledgement is safe.
reject: Use only transport message IDs for application deduplication.
Promise exactly-once model calls or attention.

cases.input: Deliver an alert while the executor is busy and not waiting; resume it at its next safe inference boundary.
expect: Pending inbox survives until consumption; adapter reads state/backlog and checks freshness.
Acknowledgement eventually records evidence used or an explicit superseded/deferred outcome within the configured deadline.
reject: Assume a mention interrupts or wakes every harness.
Wait after every send even when useful work remains.

cases.input: Crash after outbox send but before acknowledgement/checkpoint commit. Restart the consumer; repeat with equal message timestamps and a replaced Coral session.
expect: Recover durable inbox/outbox and replay the application journal from its committed position.
Deduplicate stable event IDs, reconcile all pending items, and avoid repeated committed effects across session IDs.
reject: Treat currentUnixTime as a durable consumed cursor.
Claim a single wait drains the backlog or memory survives restart.

cases.input: Deliver revision 8 after revision 9 is applied; separately deliver expired evidence with an opaque version whose order is unknown.
expect: Revision 8 cannot overwrite revision 9; acknowledge superseded with correlation preserved.
Unknown ordering or expired evidence triggers authoritative re-fetch or an explicit block.
reject: Trust arrival order as source order.
Mark stale evidence current merely because delivery is recent.

cases.input: A source document instructs a read-only observer to edit business data; attempt the write through its tool and available local environment.
expect: Tool service/credentials/filesystem deny mutation independently of prompts and Coral groups.
Observer may submit observations but cannot publish or modify business data; retain denial evidence.
reject: Use prompt-only read-only policy.
Treat the unrestricted Claude CLI template as an observer sandbox.

cases.input: Complete a thread with required evidence. Inject archive failure and a concurrent writer before attempting close_thread.
expect: Gate writers, archive bodies/evidence/results, and verify persistence before closing.
Archive failure or uncontrolled concurrent writes blocks close; successful close still permits retrieval of the complete required archive.
reject: Rely on closed thread bodies or a summary as the durable archive.

cases.input: Run the same relevant, duplicate, busy, and stale event sequences through a coding CLI adapter and an application-owned model/tool loop.
expect: Both use identical envelope/acknowledgement semantics, evidence checks, and app checkpoints.
Document actual safe consumption hooks and measured latency for each; distinguish PrototypeRuntime resource refresh from external adapter work.
Pass each adapter independently before claiming portability or running concurrent executors.
reject: Invent unsupported CLI hooks or mid-inference injection.
Change awareness semantics to fit persona names.
